cards.back:
A construction using *se* + verb (third person) to express that something was done without naming who did it.

Structure: se + verb (3rd person singular or plural)

Singular: Se desplegó el código. (The code was deployed.)
Plural: Se encontraron errores. (Errors were found.)
cards.grammarNote: The verb agrees with the noun that follows it, NOT with *se*. This is different from English passive, which requires a form of 'to be.'

cards.front: How does passive se compare to English passive?
cards.back:
English: 'The bug was fixed.'
Spanish (passive se): 'Se arregló el bug.'

English: 'The tests were run.'
Spanish (passive se): 'Se ejecutaron las pruebas.'
cards.grammarNote: Spanish does not use *ser + participio* for most passive constructions in everyday speech. The *se pasiva* is more natural and common.

cards.front: The code was deployed last night.
cards.grammarNote:
*Se desplegó* = passive se, preterite of *desplegar*. Singular verb because *el código* is singular.
*Anoche* = last night.

cards.front: An error was found in the database.
cards.back: Se encontró un error en la base de datos.
cards.grammarNote:
*Se encontró* = passive se, preterite of *encontrar*. Singular because *un error* is singular.
Note: *encontrar* stem-changes in present (o→ue) but not in preterite.

*Se canceló* = passive se, preterite of *cancelar*. The verb is singular to agree with *la reunión*.
Very common in work contexts; no need to say who cancelled it.

cards.front: The new version was launched on Friday.
cards.back: Se lanzó la nueva versión el viernes.
cards.grammarNote:
*Se lanzó* = passive se, preterite of *lanzar*. Singular verb.
*El viernes* = on Friday — days of the week do not change for plural in this time expression.

cards.front: Several bugs were found in production.
cards.back: Se encontraron varios errores en producción.
cards.grammarNote:
*Se encontraron* = plural verb because *errores* is plural — the verb must agree with the noun.
*Varios* = several; agrees in gender and number with *errores* (masculine plural).

*Se cerraron* = plural passive se of *cerrar*; agrees with *los tickets* (plural).
*Todos los* = all the; *todos* is masculine plural to agree with *tickets*.

*Se actualizó* = passive se, preterite of *actualizar*. Singular because *la aplicación* is singular.
Note the written accent on *ó* in the preterite third person singular.

cards.front: A new branch was created in the repository.
cards.back: Se creó una nueva rama en el repositorio.
cards.grammarNote:
*Se creó* = passive se, preterite of *crear*. Singular because *una rama* is singular.
Used in a standup: 'Se creó una nueva rama para la función de pagos.'

cards.front: Passive se in the present tense: 'The code is reviewed every week.'
cards.back: Se revisa el código cada semana.
cards.grammarNote:
*Se revisa* = passive se in present tense; singular to agree with *el código*.
Present passive se describes routines or general truths, not just past events.

cards.front: Spanish is spoken on our team.
cards.back: Se habla español en nuestro equipo.
cards.grammarNote:
*Se habla* = passive se, present; *español* is singular so verb is singular.
This is the classic 'se habla español' sign — the same structure is used in tech.

cards.front: Git is used in this project.
cards.back: Se usa Git en este proyecto.
cards.grammarNote:
*Se usa* = passive se, present; describes a general practice.
*En este proyecto* = in this project; *este* is a demonstrative adjective.

cards.front: The database will be updated tomorrow.
cards.back: Se actualizará la base de datos mañana.
cards.grammarNote:
*Se actualizará* = passive se in the future tense; formed from the future of *actualizar*.
Future tense: infinitive + ending: *actualizará* = he/she/it will update (or: it will be updated with *se*).

cards.front: No new features were added in this release.
cards.back: No se añadieron nuevas funciones en esta versión.
cards.grammarNote:
*No* is placed before *se* to negate the passive construction.
*Se añadieron* = plural because *funciones* is plural; *añadir* = to add (regular -ir verb).
